record.title: gui_strays exempts burst-launched uid-1001 processes from the stray kill using the client-declared _NET_WM_PID window property
record.description: At GUI-burst close, AgentBox._stop_gui_strays collects uid-1001 processes and the set of window-owning pids and calls gui_strays. A new (non-baseline, non-exec-rooted) uid-1001 process that lives in a session that existed at burst start (base_sids) is spared whenever it is 'windowed', i.e. its own pid is in window_pids, or a NON-baseline ancestor's pid is in window_pids. window_pids are produced by `xdotool getwindowpid`, which returns the _NET_WM_PID property each X client sets for itself. A burst's own GUI clients can therefore declare which pids count as window owners (including a headless background child's pid), so background work launched during the burst can survive the close and keep modifying /workspace outside any monitored burst, weakening the N-1 partial mitigation. (Children of a PRE-EXISTING windowed baseline app are still killed, because the ancestor clause requires the windowed ancestor to be non-baseline; the surviving path needs a newly-created windowed ancestor in a baseline session, or direct _NET_WM_PID membership.)
record.claimed_root_cause: Window ownership used to exempt a process is derived from a client-settable X property (_NET_WM_PID via xdotool getwindowpid) rather than a control-plane-verifiable link, so target-controlled GUI clients decide which of their processes are treated as windowed apps/helpers.

trace.description: Burst close ingests attacker-influenced container output: calls desktop_processes(sid) to get the process list and window pids, then gui_strays to classify which new uid-1001 processes to kill.
Window pids come from `xdotool search --onlyvisible --name .` then `xdotool getwindowpid $w`, i.e. the client-set _NET_WM_PID property, parsed into the wins set at line 692.

A new baseline-session process is marked windowed (p.pid in window_pids, or a non-baseline ancestor pid in window_pids) and consequently NOT appended to the kill list at lines 223-224, so it survives the burst close.

evidence.description: wins = {int(x) ...} parsed from container-side xdotool getwindowpid output; the exemption input is fully attacker/target-controlled.
windowed = p.pid in window_pids or any(a.pid in window_pids and a.pid not in baseline for a in ancestors(p)); windowed -> not killed.

Docstring states windowed apps and their helpers (and burst-start processes and docker-exec-launched tools) are intentionally left running; confirms the exemption is by design and that its only gate is window ownership.

blockers: Reachability in agentbox-desktop:0.1: whether, using only GUI tools (click/type/key), a prompt-injected agent can cause a uid-1001 process to run in a session that existed at burst start (base_sids) AND either own a visible window reported by `xdotool getwindowpid`/_NET_WM_PID or be the child of such a newly-created windowed process. The image's session semantics (whether launcher/terminal/WM-spawned apps inherit a burst-start session id vs. get a new setsid session, which line 218 kills regardless) and _NET_WM_PID behaviour are not observable from source. A pure-function harness over the real gui_strays confirms the exemption logic but cannot establish this live process/window layout.

Whether such a spared process (or its surviving background child) continues to modify /workspace after _close_gui_burst pops the burst, i.e. outside any monitored burst, so that changes escape the gui_changes manifest diff.

validation_plan.local: In a disposable, network-less agentbox-desktop:0.1 sandbox: open a GUI burst with a GUI tool call. Using GUI input only, (a) from a launcher/terminal that belongs to a burst-start session, start a GUI app that opens a visible window and whose background child appends a timestamp to a dummy file /workspace/_v15_probe every ~2s; and (b) separately start a client that sets _NET_WM_PID of its window to the background child's pid. Just before close, record `ps -eo pid=,ppid=,sid=,uid=,args=` and `for w in $(xdotool search --onlyvisible --name .); do xdotool getwindowpid $w; done` to capture the real session ids and window-pid set, and feed them through the verified gui_strays harness to predict survivors. Let the burst close on idle; then read the gui_processes_stopped audit entry and check whether /workspace/_v15_probe's mtime keeps advancing after close. Non-destructive: touches only the dummy probe file; kill the probe and discard the sandbox afterward.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner reproduces the same probe on the live deployed image/config to confirm the image's session-id and _NET_WM_PID semantics and that a spared process (or its child) modifies /workspace after burst close; collect the gui_processes_stopped and gui_changes audit entries and the manifest diff as evidence. Fix check: exempt only burst-start (baseline) processes and control-plane docker-exec-launched components, deriving ownership from a control-plane-verifiable link (e.g. the exec/ancestry already tracked) rather than the client-declared _NET_WM_PID. Non-destructive: dummy file only.
